overview.title: SchemaCraft architecture
overview.oneLiner: A Windows desktop app that reads a SQL Server catalog, draws it as an editable ER diagram, saves it as a .scraft file and exports it to SVG, HTML, PNG and PDF.
paragraphs: SchemaCraft is a Tauri 2 app. The UI is React 19 and TypeScript running in WebView2. All disk, network and OS work is done in Rust. The Rust side has two parts: a thin host (src-tauri) that exposes 21 IPC commands, and a framework-free library (crates/schemacraft-core) that holds the real logic.

Dependencies point one way: frontend -> IPC -> host -> core -> external systems. The frontend reaches Rust and the window only through src/shared/ipc, the one folder that imports the Tauri API, and ESLint enforces the layer rules (ADR-031). Commands are thin adapters: they resolve inputs, call the core and map errors, with no domain logic, and they keep blocking work off the main thread (ADR-032). The core knows nothing about Tauri or the UI. The types that cross the boundary are written once in Rust and generated as TypeScript with ts-rs.

SchemaCraft has no database of its own. SQL Server is only read, with fixed SELECT queries over sys.* views. What lasts lives in four places: .scraft files the user picks, preferences.json in %APPDATA%\com.jmanuelsoberano.schemacraft, passwords in Windows Credential Manager, and two localStorage keys for UI conveniences. The local diagnostic log, counts and timings only, lives in %LOCALAPPDATA%\com.jmanuelsoberano.schemacraft\logs and is never sent anywhere (ADR-041). Everything else is memory only.

layers.name: Frontend: app shell
layers.summary: Composition root. Lays out the window, mounts every dialog once, owns the action registry and keyboard routing.

components.name: Entry point
components.responsibility: Loads the variable Inter and JetBrains Mono faces for the UI and the static 400 and 600 faces that the exporter measures and embeds, then the React Flow CSS, tokens.css and base.css. Installs the DEV hooks and mounts <App/>. App.tsx syncs the theme and <html lang>.

components.name: AppShell and regions
components.responsibility: Lays out TopBar, the entities panel and the Inspector on either side of DiagramCanvas, and StatusBar; the panel, the canvas and the Inspector come from features/canvas and features/inspector and only get placed here, each side panel in a named aside landmark that turns inert while collapsed, with a PanelResizer from shared/ui (the Inspector's goes in through the panel's resizer slot) and its width in settingsStore; fitSidePanels (sidePanelWidths.ts) narrows the open panels in a window too narrow for both, the Inspector last and neither below its minimum, so the canvas keeps 320 px and the top bar stays in the window, without changing the remembered widths. TopBar shows LayoutMenu; its segmented control and its theme and language menus run the registry's view.detail*, settings.theme.* and settings.language.* actions, and its Inspector toggle runs view.toggleInspector. Hands DiagramCanvas the WelcomeOverlay as emptyState and the DEV hook exposeFlowInstance as onFlowInit, the sidebar the AccessBar through its notice slot (with focusEntitiesSearch as its onDismissed), and the InspectorPanel the toggle's shortcut hint and the registry's view.accessReport action for its 'Why?' links, so none of them imports app/ or features/access; the sidebar shows one muted footer while the object list may be incomplete and a neutral state for an empty schema. Mounts ConnectionDialog, ExportDialog, AboutDialog, AccessReportDialog, CommandPalette, UnsavedChangesDialog and CanvasContextMenu once, giving the context menu the registry's diagram.showAll action with its shortcut. StatusBar adds the access chip and the read-only chip, and leaves out a count of zero under partial coverage. Runs useKeyboardShortcuts, useDesktopShellGuards and useProjectWindow (window title, close guard). Calls preferencesStore.load() on mount.
patterns: Dialogs read their own open flag from a store
Props carry only the action registry
Notice slot instead of a feature import
Shell concerns reach the canvas as props
Side panels as named landmarks, inert while closed

components.name: WelcomeOverlay
components.responsibility: Empty-canvas screen. AppShell passes it to DiagramCanvas as emptyState, shown while no project is open. Offers Connect and Open through the action registry, lists recentProjects from preferencesStore and opens one with projectStore.openProject(path). Shows the developer credit.
patterns: Empty state that offers the next step

components.name: Action registry and shortcuts
components.responsibility: 33 AppActions (id, labelKey, icon, shortcut, isAvailable, unavailableReason, run) built in useAppActions.ts. A disabled action says why in its tooltip: no project, a layout running, nothing hidden, nothing to undo or redo, or a read-only project (Save, Save as and Refresh). view.accessReport (Ctrl+Shift+A) opens the Access report whenever a project is open. Since 1.1 the detail levels (view.detailCompact, view.detailKeys and view.detailFull on Ctrl+1, Ctrl+2 and Ctrl+3), the themes (settings.theme.*) and the languages (settings.language.*) are actions too, run by the top bar, and view.toggleInspector (Ctrl+I) opens or closes the Inspector with focus; the per-entity gestures and Enter on a card stay outside the registry on purpose (ADR-008). Since 1.2 help.openLogFolder opens the folder of the diagnostic log from the palette, without a shortcut, and is unavailable when the session writes no log. useKeyboardShortcuts.ts routes keys in the capture phase; the first match wins. useAppActions.test.ts builds the registry as the shell does and fails when two actions share a shortcut or one takes a browser key that is not on the claimed list. The toolbar, the menus, the welcome screen and the command palette all read this registry.

components.name: Command palette
components.responsibility: Ctrl+K palette over every registry action and every entity of the open project (listEntities from features/schema). Each entity row shows its kind: the Glasses icon and a View label in the view colour, or the table icon and Table, then schema.name and 'Center on screen'; the placeholder names commands, tables and views. paletteSearch.ts ranks results. It lives in app/ because it reads the action registry.

components.name: Desktop shell guards
components.responsibility: Inside the desktop app only (isDesktopRuntime from shared/ipc): blocks the browser context menu and dragstart outside editable fields, and middle-click autoscroll everywhere (ADR-026).

components.name: Design tokens
components.responsibility: tokens.css holds every token and is the only place a colour is written: light-dark() in oklch, the semantic tones, the view tokens (--color-view, --color-view-subtle, --color-on-view). tokens.test.ts recomputes the export palette (features/export/svg/palette.ts) from the tokens through OKLab and fails on drift, and reads every CSS Module and viewer.css as text to refuse a raw hex or oklch() colour (ADR-037). base.css holds the reset, focus ring, reduced motion and React Flow theming.

components.name: Development hooks
components.responsibility: DEV builds only: exposes the stores, the access report store included, and the React Flow instance on window.__schemacraft so scripts over CDP can drive the app. AppShell passes exposeFlowInstance to DiagramCanvas as onFlowInit, so the canvas never imports this module.

layers.name: Frontend: shared
layers.summary: Code every feature may use. It never imports from src/app or src/features, and ESLint enforces it (ADR-031).

components.name: IPC backends and resolver
components.responsibility: The only folder that imports the Tauri API. One typed backend per area (connection, project, preferences, credentials, export), each with a Tauri, an unavailable and a DEV-only preview implementation picked by createBackendResolver. Every command goes through invokeCommand, which normalises rejections with toOperationError. nativeWindow.ts wraps the window (theme, title, close guard, destroy), runtime.ts tells whether the page runs in the desktop app, and appInfo.ts with useAppInfo wraps get_app_info and open_log_folder. previewAccess.ts follows the Rust access verdicts and the refresh merge for the preview backends, whose server names choose what the login sees (ADR-014).

components.name: Error presentation
components.responsibility: describeOperationError turns an OperationError into a title, a hint and a remedy in the current language. The optional context says what the user tried, such as signing in with the Windows account. Connection, export and project use it.
patterns: Rust classifies, the UI words the remedy (ADR-012)

components.name: Internationalisation
components.responsibility: en.ts is the reference catalogue; es.ts is typed as MessageCatalog. useI18n() and translate(locale, key). translator.ts holds createCatalogTranslator, which builds t, tCount and template over any catalogue with formatMessage and Intl.PluralRules and no store behind it: useI18n builds it over the whole catalogue of the chosen language, and the exported viewer over the subset embedded in its file, so both say the same words (ADR-007). messages/rules/en.ts and es.ts hold the words of the readable rules (englishRuleMessages, RuleMessageKey), spread into en.ts and es.ts, so they are part of MessageKey and the exported viewer embeds them by the rule. prefix (ADR-039). formatMessage.ts also has formatMessageParts, which splits a template into text and the arguments of its placeholders, so a sentence can draw a column as a chip without concatenation. catalogs.test.ts checks keys, empty messages and placeholders, the viewer's and the rules' strings included. formatDate.ts formats the UTC timestamps Rust sends in the current language.

components.name: Settings store
components.responsibility: Theme preference, locale, sidebar open and width, the Inspector's width (never whether it is open) and the signatures of the partial-access notices the user closed (50 at most, most recent first), persisted in localStorage 'schemacraft.settings'. SIDEBAR_WIDTH_LIMITS (220 to 560, default 280) and INSPECTOR_WIDTH_LIMITS (280 to 560, default 360), typed with PanelResizer's PanelWidthLimits, bound both widths through clampPanelWidth. mergePersistedSettings checks every stored field and falls back to its default. useThemeSynchronization sets data-theme and the native window theme.
patterns: zustand persist with partialize and validating merge

components.name: UI primitives
components.responsibility: Accessible primitives built on Radix: Button, IconButton, Dialog, Select, SegmentedControl, RadioMenu, Tooltip, Alert (optionally announced politely, with an icon and a dismiss button), PanelResizer (the handle of both side panels) and more. No '@/' imports (imports.test.ts checks it); all text comes in through props.

components.name: PanelResizer
components.responsibility: Handle on the edge of a side panel, used by the entities panel (edge 'end') and by the Inspector (edge 'start'). Drag it to resize, use the arrow keys in steps of 16 px (away from the panel widens it on either side), Home and End for the narrowest and widest width, double-click to return to the default. Controlled and text-free: it reports the width it was dragged or stepped to, and the owner (AppShell) clamps and remembers it through settingsStore's setSidebarWidth and setInspectorWidth with SIDEBAR_WIDTH_LIMITS and INSPECTOR_WIDTH_LIMITS. It declares the PanelWidthLimits type those limits use, so it imports nothing from settingsStore; AppShell passes the limits fitSidePanels narrowed, so aria-valuemax and End follow the room the window leaves. role=separator with aria-valuenow and aria-controls.
patterns: Pointer drag with a keyboard equivalent

components.name: Brand
components.responsibility: Logo.tsx and credits.ts (DEVELOPER_NAME 'Manuel Soberano', REPOSITORY_URL), used by the shell, the welcome screen and About.

layers.name: Frontend: features
layers.summary: One folder per product capability. Stateful features own one zustand store; schema is a pure helper module; inspector holds no state and follows the canvas selection; canvas edits go through projectStore.updateCanvas. Logic lives in pure, unit-tested modules.

components.name: connection
components.responsibility: Connection dialog: form, recent connections, test, database and schema pick, inspection with progress and cancel, refresh with diff review, remembered passwords, and the 'Trust the certificate and retry' remedy. Choosing a database calls describeDatabase: the schemas to offer and the predicted access, which AccessCheckNotice shows at the end of the database section (a danger notice, with 'Read schema' disabled, when the login sees nothing). A read that finds nothing visible is blocked (blockedInspection) and creates no project. A review is up to date only when isUpToDate says so; ReviewChangesPanel also lists keys to invisible tables, not-checked facts with the date they were read and facts now available. connectionStore.ts is a phase machine (idle, testing, loadingSchemas, inspecting, reviewing, applying) and never refreshes a read-only project. fromSavedConnection.ts turns a saved connection back into a draft, live settings, a description and a history key, naming the server with formatTarget, the mirror of Rust format_target (ADR-011). The draft persists in localStorage 'schemacraft.connection' without the password.

components.name: project
components.responsibility: The open project: open, save, save as, undo and redo, unsaved-changes guard. projectStore.ts is the Memento caretaker (HISTORY_LIMIT 100) and runs ensurePlaced on every open, inspection and refresh. Opening reads an OpenedProject: a read-only project (a newer format, ADR-035) can be rearranged but is never marked unsaved and never saved, and savedWith names its writer. contentOf keeps the unknown root keys and drops the header keys. savedConnection.ts turns connection settings into the SavedConnection a project records, so project never imports connection. The window title and the close guard live in useProjectWindow.

components.name: useProjectWindow
components.responsibility: Inside the desktop app only; AppShell runs it. Keeps the window title as 'name – SchemaCraft', with a '• ' prefix while there are unsaved changes, or just 'SchemaCraft' with no project. When the window is closed with unsaved changes it cancels the close, runs guardUnsavedChanges and then closes the window for good. It reaches the window through shared/ipc/nativeWindow.ts.

components.name: ProjectNotice
components.responsibility: Non-blocking alert over the canvas when opening or saving a project fails. DiagramCanvas renders it. It reads projectStore.failure, describes the error with describeOperationError from shared/errors and clears it with dismissFailure.
patterns: Error shown where the work happens

components.name: projectPaths
components.responsibility: projectDisplayName (file name without .scraft) and projectDirectory. The window title, TopBar, WelcomeOverlay and UnsavedChangesDialog use them.

components.name: canvas
components.responsibility: Diagram state transforms (canvasState.ts), geometry, edges, nodes, context menu, transient UI store (canvasUiStore.ts), canvas commands (canvasActions.ts), layouts/ (layered with ELK in a worker, organic with d3-force, radial) and, since 1.1, the two canvas regions the shell places: DiagramCanvas and EntitiesSidebar, with entitiesSearch.ts. The saved diagram state lives in projectStore; canvas commands change it through updateCanvas: setHidden serves the sidebar eye and the context menu, setCollapsed the card chevron. canvasUiStore also holds whether the Inspector is open and its request for focus (openInspector, closeInspector, toggleInspector), and a FocusRequest can select without panning (center: false), which 'Show details' uses; canvasFocus.ts moves focus between the canvas and the Inspector (focusEntityNode, returnFocusFromInspector), the one place that knows how React Flow names a card. edgeGeometry.ts holds the one marker table (RELATION_MARKER_SHAPES, named by meaning: many, one and zeroOrOne, each drawn facing its table and turned by MARKER_ORIENT), startMarkerKind, endMarkerKind and relationPath, shared with the SVG renderer; relationMarkerIds.ts names the canvas markers. graph.ts relationEnds picks both ends of a key from the rule reader's foreignKeyChildCardinality and foreignKeyOptionality, so the standard crow's foot notation never contradicts the sentences (ADR-039), and RelationEdgeData carries the ends and the cached explanation. A self-reference loops from the referencing row to the referenced row; when its ends share a point, each moves LOOP_SPREAD off it, the referencing end up and the referenced end down. canvasUiStore holds the rule the Inspector points at (ruleHighlight: owner, columns by entity, edge id), which only its owner, closeInspector or a real change of selection clears; EntityNode reads only its own entry, outlines the card and tints the rule's rows, and RelationEdge emphasises the key's line and adds the ON DELETE sentence to its hover label, under 'When enabled:' for a disabled key. EntityNode draws a view with the Glasses icon, the VIEW label and the view tokens, and shows the collapse chevron only when isCollapsible finds rows to hide (ADR-036). describeEntities counts the columns of keys to invisible tables as key columns, so they keep the key badge without an edge.
patterns: Strategy as tagged union + exhaustive switch (ADR-022)
Geometry from data, not the DOM (ADR-020)

components.name: DiagramCanvas
components.responsibility: The one React Flow instance. Derives nodes and edges from projectStore and writes drags and the viewport back through updateCanvas; the card chevron runs canvasActions.setCollapsed. When loadToken changes it lays out a fresh project (no path, never saved, not dirty, layout manual); otherwise it restores the saved viewport or fits the diagram to the window. What belongs to the shell arrives as props: emptyState (the welcome screen), shown while no project is open, and onFlowInit (the DEV hook), called when React Flow is ready. The selection is the one source of what the Inspector shows: a double-click on a card (not on its chevron) opens the Inspector and leaves focus on the card, and Enter on a focused card opens it and hands it focus, handled here and only when the card itself is focused, so the buttons inside a card keep Enter. The React Flow root is focusable by script (tabIndex -1) for when the Inspector hands focus back and the card is not rendered, and returnFocusFromInspector is installed once; a focus request pans only when it asks to (center). Shows ProjectNotice when opening or saving fails. With a project open but no table or view, it shows a neutral empty state whose reason (an empty database, the schema selection, nothing visible to this login) comes from emptySchemaReason in schema/coverage.ts. The minimap tints views with the view colour.
patterns: Request counters (fitRequest, focusRequest) drive imperative view calls

components.name: EntitiesSidebar
components.responsibility: The entities panel. groupEntities(listEntities(snapshot)) gives the schema groups and their Tables and Views sections; entityListShape, decided on the unfiltered list, says which levels to show (several schemas, both kinds), so the structure stays put while typing. Headers are buttons with aria-expanded; a schema or a section collapses for the session only, and everything is expanded, with the toggles disabled, while the search has text. Counts read 'shown / total' once something is hidden. Each row centres its entity on click, opens the Inspector on double-click (never for a hidden entity, which has no card to select), opens the context menu and toggles visibility through canvasActions.setHidden; views carry the Glasses icon in the view colour. Keeps the empty states (no project, the emptySchemaReason states, no matches), the single not-visible footer of ADR-034 and the notice slot; the search box id comes from entitiesSearch.ts.
patterns: Shape decided on the unfiltered list
Notice slot instead of a feature import

components.name: entitiesSearch
components.responsibility: focusEntitiesSearch, run by the view.searchEntities action (Ctrl+F). Opens the entities panel if it is collapsed, then focuses and selects its search box on the next tick, once the panel is no longer inert.
patterns: Focus through a shared element id

components.name: canvasState.ensurePlaced
components.responsibility: Gives every table and view of the snapshot a NodeState. Missing ones get grid positions below the existing diagram; states of entities that no longer exist are dropped. Returns the same object when nothing changes. projectStore calls it on open, on inspection and on refresh, so the other canvas helpers can assume every entity has a node.

components.name: layouts/elkWorker.ts
components.responsibility: createElkInWorker: elkjs with a workerFactory, so a large layered layout never blocks pan and zoom. Vite serves elkjs's elk-worker.min.js as an asset from the app's own origin, which the CSP allows. canvasActions.ts keeps one worker for the lifetime of the window (ADR-022).
patterns: Heavy work off the UI thread

components.name: export
components.responsibility: Export dialog and store. ExportSpecificationBuilder validates choices. svg/renderDiagram.ts draws the SVG with the marker table of canvas/edgeGeometry.ts, the ends relationEnds picks (sc-many, sc-one and sc-zero-or-one, each with an -active variant) and the labels the caller passes (RenderOptions.labels: the VIEW label, which exportStore translates in the interface language); a view card gets the view tint, the Glasses symbol, the label pill and a secondary schema text, as on the canvas; each column name carries its full name in data-column, for the viewer's rule highlight. svg/palette.ts is the sRGB derivation of tokens.css (PALETTE_TOKENS, checked by src/app/styles/tokens.test.ts), and viewerPaletteStyles() writes it as --sc-* custom properties that html/buildStandalonePage puts before the viewer's stylesheet. html/ builds the standalone page; html/viewerMessages.ts picks, by key prefix, the subset of the catalogue the file embeds for the viewer (ViewerData.messages, the rule words included) and viewerMessages.test.ts checks it; fontFaces.ts supplies the fonts that are measured and embedded. visibleProjection is an allowlist: the visible tables, views and keys, the keys to invisible tables of visible tables, the access verdicts (AccessSummary: level and coverage, never the probe or the database user) and, apart from the snapshot, the kept facts of the objects on the diagram with their read dates (ViewerData.carriedOver), a key's only while the key itself is exported, never a hidden table's facts or unknown keys. A partial capture adds a one-line note: a footnote in SVG, PDF and PNG (RenderOptions.footnote, included in the measured size) and a header line in the HTML viewer. Only the document string goes to Rust.
patterns: Allowlist of what leaves the app

components.name: fontFaces.ts
components.responsibility: The four static faces the diagram uses: Inter and JetBrains Mono at 400 and 600, from @fontsource. main.tsx loads them, and buildDocument waits for document.fonts so text is measured with them. With embedFonts (SVG and HTML only) loadEmbeddedFontFaces fetches the bundled WOFF2 files once and inlines them as base64 @font-face rules; a failed fetch is retried on the next export.

components.name: preferences
components.responsibility: Mirror of the Rust-owned preferences.json: recent connections and recent projects. Applies the whole document Rust returns.

components.name: about
components.responsibility: About dialog: name, version, credit, repository URL, and the Diagnostic log row (DiagnosticLog.tsx): the folder from AppInfo.logDirectory, Open log folder, the sentence that the log holds counts and timings and is never sent anywhere, the states for no folder and for a browser preview, and the failure to open it. aboutStore.openLogFolder, shared with the help.openLogFolder action, opens the dialog with the failure.

components.name: access
components.responsibility: Graded disclosure of partial access (ADR-034). accessCause.ts orders the causes (nothing visible for lack of a grant or behind a possible DENY, an empty database, explicit DENYs, denials the login cannot see, no VIEW DEFINITION on the database or on some schemas, objects that may be missing) and says whether a GRANT helps; grantScript.ts writes the least-privilege GRANT VIEW DEFINITION script with comments in the user's language and the SQL Server 2022 disclosure; accessNotice.ts decides when the chip and the bar show and signs a notice by endpoint, database and verdicts. AccessChip (status bar), AccessBar (dismissible, above the entities list) and AccessReportDialog (view.accessReport, Ctrl+Shift+A) read snapshot.access of the open project; accessReportStore holds the dialog's open flag. CopyScriptButton copies the script; SchemaCraft never runs it. AccessCheckNotice lives in features/connection and uses these pure helpers, so the dependency points one way.

components.name: schema
components.responsibility: Pure helpers over SchemaSnapshot: formatDataType and describeColumn (dataType.ts), which prints 'DEFAULT (not available)' or '(default not recorded)' instead of dropping a default it cannot read; the one home of entity identity (entities.ts): EntityKind, ENTITY_KINDS, entityKey, listEntities, groupEntities (schemas, then Tables and Views sections), filterEntityGroups, countEntities and entityListShape; definitionText and isUnknownDefinition (definition.ts), the only readers of the raw Definition statuses; objectsCoverage, definitionsCoverage, listsEveryObject, emptySchemaReason and the export-safe AccessSummary (coverage.ts); quoteIdentifier (sqlIdentifiers.ts); foreignKeyId (entities.ts), the id of a key's relationship on the canvas, in the SVG and in the details; objectDetails.ts (describeObjectDetails: the facts of one table or view with how far the capture vouches for each, FactText and ListCompleteness, each CHECK's reading and each key's explanation) and objectDetailsView.ts (presentObjectDetails: the same as translated text, DetailsView, with a RuleView per CHECK and key and the notes of each section), the view-model the Inspector and the viewer's detail panel share (ADR-038). rules/ holds the readable rules (ADR-039): checkTokens.ts (tokenizeCheck), checkParser.ts (parseCheck, recursive descent with T-SQL precedence) and checkReader.ts (readCheckConstraint over the stored text: a closed set of forms read all or nothing, as a CheckReading that is read, unread, notAvailable or notRecorded); foreignKeyReader.ts (foreignKeyOptionality, foreignKeyChildCardinality, explainForeignKey and explainForeignKeyToInvisibleTable, foreignKeyExplanations cached per snapshot in a WeakMap, ExplanationScope and foreignKeyDefinitionSql); and ruleText.ts (RuleNode trees of message keys with typed arguments, and formatRuleText, which turns them into text, column, table and code parts). The golden forms of crates/schemacraft-core/tests/fixtures/sqlserver/check_forms.json drive checkReader.test.ts. No store, no React. A leaf: ESLint lets it import only shared/ (contracts and i18n) and itself, so every feature and the viewer bundle can import it (ADR-037).
patterns: Leaf module, enforced by lint, safe for the viewer bundle
Interpreter over a closed grammar with conservative fallback (ADR-039)

components.name: inspector
components.responsibility: The Inspector panel (ADR-038): the details of the selected table or view beside the canvas. InspectorPanel.tsx reads the snapshot, the canvas nodes and the inspection options from projectStore and the selection, the focus request and closeInspector from canvasUiStore; inspectorScope.ts builds the DetailsScope (hidden keys, the coverage from accessSummary, the carried facts, the schema filter) and inspectedKey picks the one selected entity, so none or several selected is an empty state. It memoises describeObjectDetails and presentObjectDetails with useI18n's translator. A permanent header (the title and a close button with the Ctrl+I hint) gives the empty states a focus target; the entity heading takes focus on a focus request; the resizer the shell passes in (resizer slot) is drawn inside the element that handles Escape, so Escape anywhere in the panel, the handle included, runs focusEntityNode and leaves the panel open. InspectorSections.tsx draws the DetailsView as the viewer does, one component per section kind, with count chips, the one honest empty line and the referenced-by footnote; a relation target with a key is a link that runs focusEntity then openInspector; a value the capture could not vouch for carries an icon and its hint, and a not-available value, a not-visible target and a not-visible empty line add a 'Why?' link that opens the Access report through the action the shell passes in. RuleItem.tsx draws a CHECK or a key as its sentences, with column, table and code chips and group headings, or the line that says it cannot be put into words, and a Show SQL toggle (aria-expanded, aria-controls) at the end of its head with the SQL, its note and Copy SQL behind it; an unread CHECK starts with its SQL open, and sqlDisclosure.ts starts the toggle over when a refresh changes the rule's SQL or its readability; the panel keys its sections by entity, so another table's rules get items of their own. Hovering the item or focusing any of its controls calls setRuleHighlight with an owner from useId, and leaving it calls clearRuleHighlight(owner) once neither the pointer nor the focus is inside; the columns table tints the rows of the highlighted rule. A table chip opens only the item's other table and stays out of the tab order, since the target link is the keyboard's way there; each section ends with its notes (pattern, collation, derived). No store, no role=dialog; tokens only.
patterns: Follows the selection, holds no state
Highlight owned by the item that set it, no extra tab stop

layers.name: Frontend: standalone viewer
layers.summary: Vanilla TypeScript app embedded in exported HTML files. No React, no stores, no network, no catalogue of its own.

components.name: Viewer
components.responsibility: Reads the embedded JSON, draws with renderDiagramSvg, passing the VIEW label of the embedded catalogue, and offers pan and zoom, three detail levels, a search whose results name the kind (Table or View, in the view colour), neighbour highlight, a detail panel whose kind line is coloured for views, and a theme toggle. Its colours are the --sc-* properties buildStandalonePage writes from the palette; viewer.css declares none beyond its two translucent shadows. Its words are the catalogue subset embedded in the file (ViewerData.messages), read with createCatalogTranslator, so it has no catalogue of its own (ADR-007). The detail panel is the view-model of features/schema, describeObjectDetails and presentObjectDetails, with the scope of a file: no hidden entities, the embedded access verdicts and kept facts, and only the diagram known; it draws every section in the fixed order with the Inspector's words and states, for what is on the diagram: keys to tables off the diagram are not in the file (nor the FK mark they give their columns), an empty relation list reads 'None on the diagram', a list that is not empty carries no note that a key may be missing, and there is no 'Why?' link. A relation target on the diagram is a link that selects, centres and focuses the panel's heading (ADR-038). Every CHECK and key reads out as in the Inspector: rules.ts draws the RuleView (sentences with column, table and code chips, group headings) and its SQL in a <details>, open from the start for a rule that cannot be put into words, and main.ts draws the section notes (sc-rule-note); dom.ts holds h(). Pointing at or focusing a rule highlights it (ADR-039): paintRuleHighlight inserts an outline rect beside each card involved (sc-rule-outline) and a tint and a bar behind each of its rows (sc-rule-tint, sc-rule-bar), found through the SVG's data-column, marks the names and types (sc-rule-column, sc-rule-type) and the key's relation (sc-rule-relation with sc-active), and main.ts's paintRuleRows tints the panel's own rows (sc-rule-row); only the item that set it clears it, the neighbour highlight waits while it lasts, and pointer moves inside the panel are not moves over the diagram. render() replaces only the SVG and repaints the selection and the rule, so a theme, a detail level or the late fonts never take keyboard focus out of the panel. A card is selected from the press, because the stage captures the pointer and the release lands on it. Choosing a search result focuses the heading too; there is no aria-live. An export of a partial capture shows a note line under the header bar. Imports canvasState and geometry (with rowCenterY and ROW_HEIGHT for the highlight) from canvas, entityKey, the view-model and the rule part types from schema, the renderer and ViewerData from export and the translator from shared/i18n, but no React and no stores.

components.name: schemacraft-viewer-bundle plugin
components.responsibility: Serves virtual:schemacraft-viewer. Builds src/viewer/main.ts in memory as an IIFE and exports viewerScript and viewerStyles.

layers.name: IPC boundary
layers.summary: Where the webview and Rust meet: generated types, request/response calls, ordered event channels, one error envelope and the permission list.

components.name: Generated contracts
components.responsibility: TypeScript generated from Rust types by ts-rs into model/, inspectors/, diff/, project/, preferences/, credentials/, export/ and ipc/. src/shared/contracts/index.ts re-exports them. Committed, never edited by hand; CI fails on drift.

components.name: Commands (invoke)
components.responsibility: invokeCommand(name, args) in src/shared/ipc reaches one of the 21 commands in generate_handler!. Arguments go camelCase from TS and arrive as snake_case Rust parameters. Commands that only read memory stay synchronous and return at once (get_app_info, read_preferences, both cancel_* commands). Every other command is async, and its file, credential-store or heavy work runs on the blocking pool through run_blocking (ADR-032), so the window never freezes.
patterns: The signature decides the thread (async or sync)

components.name: Event channels
components.responsibility: Channel<InspectionEvent> and Channel<ExportEvent>. First event Started{jobId}, then Progress. Serialised as {event, data}.

components.name: CommandError envelope
components.responsibility: {kind: {type, value}, message}. One CommandErrorKind variant and one From impl per core error, plus UnknownJob, InvalidArgument and Unexpected (a blocking task that could not be joined), which serialise as {type} with no value. Since 1.2 each From impl also keeps the error's log_summary(): the SQL Server error number and the catalog query name, in #[serde(skip)] fields that never cross the IPC. CommandError::log(command) hands them with the kind (CommandErrorKind is a ClosedKind) to diagnostics::command_failed. commands::logged calls it for every async command, and the synchronous cancel commands call it directly (ADR-041).

components.name: Capabilities and plugins
components.responsibility: Eight entries, exactly what the frontend calls: core:default, core:window:allow-set-theme, core:window:allow-set-title, core:window:allow-destroy, dialog:allow-open, dialog:allow-save, opener:allow-reveal-item-in-dir, and opener:allow-open-url scoped to https://reactflow.dev/*, because the opener plugin's injected script opens the React Flow credit link in the browser. set-title and destroy serve the close guard in nativeWindow.ts. App commands need no entry. No fs plugin, so the frontend never touches files.

layers.name: Tauri host
layers.summary: Thin adapter. Starts the process and holds shared state. Commands resolve inputs, call the core and map errors; they hold no domain logic.

components.name: main.rs
components.responsibility: tauri::generate_context!() first, so logging::initialize opens the diagnostic log with the identifier before anything can fail, then the WebView2 check (native bilingual dialog and exit if missing; logged as startup_failed), app_started with the app and WebView2 versions, plugins dialog and opener, AppState with the log folder, the main window built by hand (optional CDP port from SCHEMACRAFT_REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT, also in release builds), and the 21 commands; a failed start is logged as startup_failed too.

components.name: Logging
components.responsibility: Two layers on one tracing registry (ADR-041). The console layer writes to stdout under SCHEMACRAFT_LOG (default info in release, info,schemacraft=debug in debug; console_directives is pure). The file layer accepts only the target schemacraft-diagnostics, from the module schemacraft_core::diagnostics (diagnostics::MODULE), at info and above, whatever SCHEMACRAFT_LOG says, and its DiagnosticFormat writes the UTC time, the level and the event's fields, never a span, a target or a thread. tracing-appender's RollingFileAppender writes schemacraft.<UTC date>.log daily, in blocking mode, and never renames a file, so two instances share a day's file. It keeps at most seven files, the panic file among them: each start and each rollover deletes the oldest, by creation time, until six are left, then opens today's. log_directory (pure) joins LOCALAPPDATA, the identifier and logs; when the folder cannot be created the console is the only output. The panic hook appends time, version and file:line, never the message, to schemacraft-panic.log through std::fs, without the logger's lock, before panic = "abort".

components.name: AppState
components.responsibility: Jobs registries ('inspection-N', 'export-N' -> CancellationToken), PreferencesStore, the credential store (SystemCredentialStore) and the folder of the diagnostic log, as logging opened it, or None. PreferencesStore applies a change to a copy and keeps it only once the file holds it, and never overwrites a file written by a newer version.

components.name: Tauri configuration
components.responsibility: Identifier com.jmanuelsoberano.schemacraft, version from package.json, window 'main' (create: false; main.rs builds it), NSIS bundle per user in English and Spanish, webviewInstallMode skip. csp: scripts only from 'self', inline styles allowed, connect-src limited to 'self' and the IPC origins. devCsp, used only by tauri dev, adds inline scripts and the Vite dev server on localhost:1420 (http and ws) for hot reload.

components.name: commands/app_info.rs
components.responsibility: get_app_info: name, version, isDebugBuild and logDirectory, the folder of the diagnostic log or null when this session writes none. Sync, reads AppState, no core call.

components.name: commands/connection.rs
components.responsibility: Async. test_connection, list_databases, describe_database and inspect_database each resolve a stored password through run_blocking, call create_inspector, then one inspector method. describe_database runs the access probe and returns a DatabaseDescription: the schemas with visible tables or views and the predicted access, reading no object. A typed password arrives inside ConnectionSettings on every call. inspect_database streams progress; cancel_inspection (sync) cancels by jobId at any point, connecting included.

components.name: commands/project.rs
components.responsibility: Async. read_project returns an OpenedProject (the project, upgraded when older, and isReadOnly) and write_project stamps savedAt and savedWith; both do their file IO through run_blocking, and so do compute_schema_diff and refresh_project_content, which handle whole snapshots.

components.name: commands/preferences.rs
components.responsibility: read_preferences is synchronous and returns the copy in memory. remember and forget for connections and projects are async and save through run_blocking; each returns the whole document as saved.

components.name: commands/credentials.rs
components.responsibility: Async, with the keyring calls on run_blocking. has_stored_password, remember_password, forget_password, keyed by SavedConnection::credential_key. remember_password receives the password once and no command sends it back (ADR-019). This does not cover typed passwords, which travel with every connection command and with each refresh from liveSettings.
patterns: Secret never serialised toward the webview (ADR-019)

components.name: commands/export.rs
components.responsibility: Async. export_diagram runs the core export through run_blocking and streams stages; cancel_export (sync) cancels by jobId. Like every command that can fail, a failure is logged by name and kind through commands::logged or CommandError::log (ADR-041).
patterns: Offload CPU work to the blocking pool

components.name: commands/diagnostics.rs
components.responsibility: Async. open_log_folder takes the folder from AppState, never from the frontend, creates it if the user deleted it and opens it with the opener plugin's Rust API (OpenerExt::open_path) on run_blocking, so no capability grows. Without a folder it fails as invalidArgument (ADR-041).

layers.name: Rust core
layers.summary: schemacraft-core: framework-free library with eight public modules. About 10.5k lines and 160 unit tests.

components.name: model
components.responsibility: Pure schema types: SchemaSnapshot, Table, View, Column, SqlDataType, PrimaryKey, Index, CheckConstraint, ForeignKey, QualifiedName. Foreign keys live on the snapshot because they are the graph edges; ForeignKeyToInvisibleTable holds the ones whose referenced table the login cannot see. Definition (readable, notVisible, notRecorded, unknown) carries CHECK and DEFAULT texts. access.rs holds AccessProbe and AccessProfile with the pure level and coverage rules; carry_over.rs holds SnapshotFact, CarriedFact and SchemaSnapshot::with_unchecked_facts_from, the merge a refresh applies. The snapshot keeps keys from newer versions in a flattened unknown map.

components.name: inspectors
components.responsibility: DatabaseInspector trait (test_connection, list_databases, describe_database, inspect), create_inspector factory, ConnectionSettings, InspectionOptions, DatabaseDescription, ProgressReporter with the CheckingAccess stage, and InspectorError with 13 variants, whose log_summary() keeps the kind, the SQL Server error number and the query name for the diagnostic log. inspect can be cancelled at any point, connecting included.

components.name: inspectors/sqlserver
components.responsibility: SQL Server strategy. settings.rs builds the tiberius Config, pool.rs is a bb8 manager opened per operation (1 or 4 sessions), access.rs holds the access probe (one batch, two result sets; no denial is counted for dbo) that describe_database and every inspection run, catalog.rs holds the named sys.* queries, assembly.rs builds the snapshot purely (unreadable texts become NotVisible, keys to invisible tables are kept apart), bound_defaults.rs reads legacy bound defaults, data_types.rs holds type rules, errors.rs maps driver errors (a TLS failure becomes UntrustedCertificate) and keeps the SQL Server error number. Every catalog query and the access probe log catalog_query, and read_snapshot logs inspection_completed with the ms of connecting, reading and assembling (ADR-041). inspect races the cancellation token with tokio::select! (biased), connecting included.

components.name: diff
components.responsibility: SchemaDiff::between(previous, current) compares the saved snapshot with the fresh one merged with what it could not check (with_unchecked_facts_from), so what the login cannot see is listed in not_checked, never as removed. Pairs tables and views by qualified name, foreign keys and keys to invisible tables by (referencing table, name), columns, indexes and checks by name; texts differ only when both are readable. Also now_available, access_changed and is_up_to_date. Sorted output. No rename detection.

components.name: project
components.responsibility: .scraft document (FORMAT_VERSION 2, MIN_READER_VERSION 2), read and written by file.rs with the fs helpers, which logs project_opened and project_saved (format, KB, ms). A newer file opens read-only when its minReaderVersion allows it and is refused otherwise; an older one is upgraded by migrations.rs on the raw JSON; unknown keys at the root, the snapshot, the canvas and each node are kept (ADR-035). ProjectContent (with_refreshed_snapshot applies the carry-over merge), SavedConnection without password, CanvasState (the Memento) with normalisation and retaining_entities_of.

components.name: fs.rs
components.responsibility: Crate-private helpers that project, preferences and export share: read_bytes tells a missing file apart, format_version reads the header of the preferences document (project files read their two version numbers themselves), and write_json_atomically and write_bytes_atomically write a sibling .tmp, flush it with sync_all and rename it over the destination.

components.name: preferences
components.responsibility: Preferences document: recent connections and recent projects, 10 each, deduplicated. The format version is checked first: a damaged file is reported as corrupt and a newer one as unsupported, and the host decides what to do with each.

components.name: credentials
components.responsibility: CredentialStore trait with SystemCredentialStore (keyring, Windows Credential Manager, service 'SchemaCraft') and InMemoryCredentialStore for tests.

components.name: export
components.responsibility: export_diagram (logged as export_written: format, KB, ms): SVG and HTML written verbatim, PNG with resvg at 1x/2x/4x (max 16384 px per side), PDF with svg2pdf. fonts.rs loads the four TTFs from crates/schemacraft-core/assets/fonts (include_bytes!) and then the system fonts for characters the Latin subsets lack, in one OnceLock database (ADR-024).

components.name: diagnostics
components.responsibility: The only emitter of the target schemacraft-diagnostics (TARGET), whose hyphen no module path has, from the module the file layer checks as well (MODULE), one function per event whose parameters are integers, booleans, durations, &'static str and ClosedKind values: app_started, startup_failed, catalog_query, inspection_completed (counts, access level, ms per stage), project_opened, project_saved, export_written and command_failed (command, kind, SQL Server error number, query). ErrorSummary is what log_summary() returns: kind, error number and query name, never the message. Depends on model alone; the other modules mark their kinds with the ClosedKind marker trait. A source scan test fails when another file names the target or imports TARGET under another name (ADR-041).

layers.name: External systems
layers.summary: Everything outside the app's own code that it reads or writes.

components.name: SQL Server (read-only)
components.responsibility: The only database the app talks to. Only its catalog is read, with the permissions of the user's login: what that login cannot see is recorded as not visible, never as absent (ADR-034). TLS mandatory by default without trusting the certificate. Sessions show program_name 'SchemaCraft' and close after each operation.

components.name: File system
components.responsibility: .scraft and export files at paths the user picks in native dialogs, preferences.json in %APPDATA%, system fonts for PNG and PDF.
patterns: Dialog returns a path, Rust does the IO

components.name: Windows Credential Manager
components.responsibility: Remembered SQL login passwords as generic credentials named '<sqlserver://server/login>.SchemaCraft'. The server part is the lower-cased display target, e.g. host,1433 or host\instance. Reached only from Rust.

components.name: WebView2 runtime
components.responsibility: Renders the UI. Not bundled; checked at startup. If missing, a native dialog offers the Microsoft download page in the default browser and the app exits.

components.name: WebView2 localStorage
components.responsibility: Two keys: 'schemacraft.settings' (theme, language, the entities panel, the Inspector's width and the closed access notices) and 'schemacraft.connection' (the last draft: the password blank, but server, login, database, schemas, encryption and trustServerCertificate kept). Both live in the WebView2 profile under %LOCALAPPDATA%\com.jmanuelsoberano.schemacraft. Neither holds a secret; deleting preferences.json clears neither, and clearing the WebView2 data resets both (ADR-017).

layers.name: Delivery
layers.summary: Pinned toolchains, CI gates, the release workflow, the smoke test of the real binary, the developer scripts, the capability probe and the check that keeps this page in step.

components.name: CI workflow
components.responsibility: On every pull request each job first runs scripts/ci-changes.sh. Windows job: the CHANGELOG entry of the package.json version (release-notes.mjs), prettier, eslint, tsc, vitest and npm run docs:check always; when code changed, also cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test, the contracts check, tauri build --no-bundle with the ci profile, WebView2 when the runner lacks it and the smoke test, uploading the exe and the screenshots. Linux job, when the core changed: the SQL Server integration tests, sqlserver_integration, sqlserver_permissions and diagnostics_privacy, against two services, mssql/server:2022-latest on port 1433 and 2019-latest on 1434, in one step per server that names the major version it must report (SCHEMACRAFT_TEST_MSSQL_MAJOR, 16 and 15); the 2019 step runs after a 2022 failure too, and SCHEMACRAFT_TEST_REQUIRE_SERVER=1 makes a missing server fail the tests instead of skipping them. Two services in the one job rather than a matrix keep the name of the required check. Pushes to main run everything and keep the cache warm (ADR-033).

components.name: Release workflow
components.responsibility: On a v* tag, without caches: checks that the tag is on main and matches package.json and Cargo.toml and that CHANGELOG.md has its entry, runs the gates, builds the exe and the NSIS installer with the full release profile, installs WebView2 when missing, runs the smoke test (screenshots uploaded), writes SHA256SUMS.txt and creates a draft GitHub release whose notes end with that entry, after what SchemaCraft is, the assets and the code signing policy (ADR-027).

components.name: Smoke test
components.responsibility: Launches the release exe with a CDP port and its own WebView2 profile (WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER), then checks the welcome screen, About, language, theme and that F5 does not reload. Saves screenshots to smoke-test/. Does not test connect, save or export.
patterns: Black-box test of the shipped binary

components.name: release-notes.mjs
components.responsibility: Prints the notes of a release: what SchemaCraft is, the assets, the code signing policy and the version's CHANGELOG.md entry with its wrapped lines joined. Fails when the entry, its date or its link is missing. release.yml publishes its output as the body of the draft release; CI runs it on every pull request for the version in package.json (ADR-027).
patterns: Release notes written once, in the changelog

components.name: Architecture page
components.responsibility: This page. index.html renders model.json in English and Spanish; GitHub Pages publishes docs/. check-architecture-page.mjs (npm run docs:check) compares the manifest with the code and checks that component paths exist and that both languages share their ids. CI and the release workflow run it; npm run docs:serve previews the page (ADR-030).
patterns: Facts as data, checked in CI

components.name: dev-sqlserver.ps1
components.responsibility: Local SQL Server containers for the integration tests: -Version 2022, the default, is schemacraft-mssql on port 14333, and -Version 2019 is schemacraft-mssql2019 on port 14334, so both run side by side as in CI. Actions: start (waits until logins work), stop, remove, env. env prints the SCHEMACRAFT_TEST_MSSQL_* variables, the major version the server must report included. The default sa password is for these containers only; SCHEMACRAFT_TEST_MSSQL_PASSWORD overrides it.

components.name: SQL Server integration tests
components.responsibility: sqlserver_integration.rs creates databases from fixtures/sqlserver/fixture.sql, changes.sql and stress_200_tables.sql, then checks connection errors (the untrusted certificate included), describe_database, inspection, progress, cancellation and refresh against a real server. It also builds SchemaCraftCheckForms from fixtures/sqlserver/check_forms.json (72 golden CHECK forms, which the rule reader's vitest suite reads too) and rule_facts.sql, asserts every stored form, column list and enabled state against the engine, and pins on scratch tables the CHECK and foreign key behaviour the rule sentences rest on (ADR-039). It also builds SchemaCraftCode from fixtures/sqlserver/code.sql (views WITH CHECK OPTION, indexed and encrypted; triggers on a table and a view, ordered, disabled, NOT FOR REPLICATION and encrypted; procedures and functions of every T-SQL kind, no CLR module; a code-only schema; a database DDL trigger) and runs the capability probe as sa on SchemaCraftFixture, SchemaCraftCheckForms and SchemaCraftCode: the output contract of tests/common (one result set, nvarchar, nvarchar, bigint, every pair in PROBE_METRICS), no failed section and the counts each fixture defines; a run while another connection holds a schema lock, in which every failed section returns only error 1222; and a static check that the script is one read-only batch, that every CATCH returns only ERROR_NUMBER(), that every label is a literal or comes from a fixed VALUES list and that it calls none of the functions that return a name, an error message or a definition, such as OBJECT_NAME, ERROR_MESSAGE or OBJECT_DEFINITION (ADR-040). sqlserver_permissions.rs seeds permissions.sql (the fixture schema, an empty database and a database with denials made to public) and creates nine low-privilege logins with permission_logins.sql (db_owner, db_datareader, VIEW DEFINITION only, reader plus a schema's VIEW DEFINITION, two tables, CONNECT only, two schema-DENY variants and a column DENY) with a password made up for the run, plus, only on SQL Server 2022 and later, a tenth with permission_logins_2022.sql (VIEW DEFINITION with VIEW SECURITY DEFINITION denied), then checks every access verdict, hidden text and refresh rule, and that a denial to public never reaches dbo. On 2019 HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME answers NULL for VIEW SECURITY DEFINITION and denials stay countable; on 2022 the tenth login sees no denial, not even its own, nor its own database user, so its denials are unknown (ADR-034). It also runs the capability probe as sa and as the owner, reader, VIEW DEFINITION, sales-texts and connect-only logins, and the tenth on 2022, and pins what each one counts, such as no procedure and no readable text for db_datareader, and its VIEW SECURITY DEFINITION answer, -1 for every login on 2019. diagnostics_privacy.rs captures every event on the diagnostics target at every level, while it reads SchemaCraftPermissions as sa and as the db_datareader login, logs in with a wrong password, opens a database the login has no user in and reads as the login of fixtures/sqlserver/diagnostics_logins.sql, which may not read sys.check_constraints; it fails on any fixture name or readable expression from an sa read, the server's name, a login, the host, a password, a database or a fragment of the server's messages, and checks the counts, kinds and error numbers 18456, 4060 and 229 (ADR-041). tests/common holds the shared helpers. The stress test must read 200 tables within 5 s (STRESS_BUDGET; the product target is 3 s) and prints its time with the server version. connects_to_the_expected_major_version, in each binary, checks that the server reports the major version SCHEMACRAFT_TEST_MSSQL_MAJOR names, so a step cannot test the wrong server; CI runs the three binaries against SQL Server 2019 and 2022, and check_forms.json and rule_facts.sql hold on both unchanged. Every test that needs the server is skipped when SCHEMACRAFT_TEST_MSSQL_HOST is not set, unless SCHEMACRAFT_TEST_REQUIRE_SERVER, which CI sets, makes it fail; the static check of the probe runs in every cargo test.
patterns: Golden table shared with the frontend tests

components.name: capability-probe.sql
components.responsibility: A read-only T-SQL batch without GO that the owner of a database the project cannot see runs in SSMS or sqlcmd, with the login SchemaCraft uses, and shares as numbers. It fills a table variable with (section, metric, value) rows, each section but probe in its own TRY ... CATCH, and returns them in one SELECT: objects per type, module texts per kind (readable, encrypted, not visible, bytes, CR, trailing spaces), DML triggers, views, parameters, index and constraint states, computed columns, descriptions, the server version as numbers, the login's permissions and timings in milliseconds. A text scan, on by default (@scan_text), counts on the server the modules with credential-like words or dynamic SQL. Labels are literals of the script and values are bigint, so no name and no text is returned; a failed section returns only its error number. It lives under crates/ so that an edit runs the SQL Server tests (ADR-033, ADR-040).

components.name: prepare-fonts.mjs
components.responsibility: Turns the static WOFF2 files of @fontsource/inter and @fontsource/jetbrains-mono into TTF with wawoff2 (a devDependency), because resvg reads only TTF and OTF. Writes them and the font licences to crates/schemacraft-core/assets/fonts, where they are committed and included with include_bytes!. Run it after bumping the font packages.

components.name: Cargo workspace and toolchain
components.responsibility: rust-toolchain.toml pins Rust 1.99.0 with rustfmt and clippy. [workspace.lints] forbids unsafe code, denies unwrap, expect, panic, todo, unimplemented and dbg_macro, and warns on missing_docs and clippy pedantic. [profile.release] sets lto, codegen-units 1, opt-level 3, panic = 'abort' and strip. With panic = 'abort' a panic ends the process at once, with no unwinding.

dataStores.name: .scraft project file
dataStores.location: Any path the user picks in the Save dialog
dataStores.format: Pretty JSON, camelCase, trailing newline, formatVersion 2 with minReaderVersion 2
dataStores.contents: Header (formatVersion, minReaderVersion, savedAt, savedWith) plus the connection without password (trustServerCertificate included), inspection options, the schema snapshot with its access profile (the permission facts, the database user name and the verdicts) and the facts kept from earlier reads, and canvas state (detail level, layout, viewport, node positions, collapsed and hidden flags).
dataStores.notes: Written atomically. A format 1 file (SchemaCraft 1.0) is upgraded in memory by migrations.rs and saved as format 2, which 1.0 cannot open. A newer file opens read-only when its minReaderVersion is 2 or less and is refused otherwise. Unknown keys at the root, the snapshot, the canvas and each node are kept and written back. The database user name stays in the file and never reaches an export. Saving the same content twice gives the same bytes apart from savedAt (and savedWith after an upgrade); nodes are sorted by qualified name.

dataStores.name: preferences.json
dataStores.owner: Rust: crates/schemacraft-core/src/preferences/mod.rs, kept in memory by src-tauri/src/state.rs
dataStores.contents: Up to 10 recent connections (no password) and up to 10 recent projects.
dataStores.notes: The frontend only mirrors it. A missing or damaged file becomes defaults. A file written by a newer version is left untouched: this version starts with an empty history and does not save changes to it.

dataStores.name: Remembered passwords
dataStores.contents: SQL login passwords the user chose to remember.
dataStores.notes: Only Rust reads them, right before connecting, and no command returns them. The server part of the name is the lower-cased display target (host,1433 or host\instance). They roam with roaming profiles.

dataStores.name: localStorage 'schemacraft.settings'
dataStores.contents: Theme preference, locale, sidebar open and sidebar width, the Inspector's width (280 to 560 px; whether it is open is never saved), and the signatures of the partial-access notices the user closed (endpoint, database, level and coverage; up to 50, most recent first).
dataStores.notes: UI convenience only, never a secret. mergePersistedSettings checks each field when it is read back and falls back to the default. Deleting preferences.json does not clear it; clearing the WebView2 data resets the theme, language and panels, and closed access notices show again (ADR-017).

dataStores.name: localStorage 'schemacraft.connection'
dataStores.contents: The last connection draft: server, authentication mode, login, remember-password flags, database, schemas, includeViews, encryption and trustServerCertificate.
dataStores.notes: partialize forces the password to ''; everything else stays after the app closes, so a trustServerCertificate = true chosen once is still set in the next session. Deleting preferences.json clears the history but not this draft; clearing the WebView2 data empties the form. ADR-017 and the README list both keys.

dataStores.name: Export files
dataStores.owner: TypeScript builds the document (src/features/export); Rust writes it (crates/schemacraft-core/src/export)
dataStores.contents: The visible diagram. HTML embeds the visible data as JSON plus the viewer code and the viewer's message subset in the export language. A partial capture adds a one-line note: a footnote in SVG, PDF and PNG, a header line in HTML.
dataStores.notes: Written atomically. HTML drops hidden tables, the connection, the server version, the access probe and the database user, and unknown keys; of the access profile it embeds only the level and the coverage, and of the facts kept from an earlier read only those of the objects and keys on the diagram, with their read dates, apart from the snapshot, so the detail panel can date them without naming a hidden table. Tables, texts and keys kept from an earlier read are drawn like any other object on the diagram.

dataStores.name: Session memory (not saved)
dataStores.contents: Undo history (100), liveSettings with the typed password (sent again on each refresh), running jobs, dialog phases, selection, zoom and whether the Inspector is open.
dataStores.notes: Lost on close. The unsaved-changes guard and the close guard protect the canvas.

dataStores.name: SQL Server catalog
dataStores.contents: Tables, views, columns, keys, indexes, checks and foreign keys, and the login's permissions (the access probe).
dataStores.notes: Read-only source. SchemaCraft never writes to it and keeps no session open. What the login cannot see is recorded as not visible, never as absent.

dataStores.name: Logs
dataStores.format: One line per event: UTC time, level, message and name=value fields
dataStores.contents: schemacraft.<UTC date>.log, one per day, at most seven files kept, the panic file among them: the typed events only, versions, counts, timings, formats, read-only flags, sizes in KB, error kinds, SQL Server error numbers and fixed query and command names. Never a server, host, login, password, database, object name, path, SQL text, definition or error message. schemacraft-panic.log: time, version and file:line of a panic. stdout keeps the console events under SCHEMACRAFT_LOG.
dataStores.notes: Local only, never sent anywhere; the about dialog shows the folder and opens it. Files are named by date and never renamed, so two instances append safely; every start and every UTC midnight first deletes the oldest files, by creation time, until six are left, then opens today's, so the panic file counts toward the seven and a second start on a day leaves six. Without the folder the console is the only output (ADR-041).

flows.name: Connect and inspect a database
flows.summary: From Ctrl+N to a laid-out diagram, with progress and cancel.

steps.detail: AppAction 'project.connect' runs guardUnsavedChanges, then connectionStore.openDialog. A recent connection can fill the form first (see the welcome and recents flow).

steps.action: Tests the connection, lists databases and describes the chosen one
steps.detail: draftToSettings builds ConnectionSettings; invoke test_connection, list_databases, then describe_database once a database is chosen: the schemas with visible tables or views and the predicted access, which AccessCheckNotice shows (nothing for full access, one line for partial access, a blocking notice when the login sees nothing). A typed password travels inside ConnectionSettings on each of these calls; an empty field with a remembered password sends {source:'stored'}.

steps.action: Resolves the password and builds the inspector
steps.detail: resolve_stored_password swaps {source:'stored'} for the secret from Credential Manager; create_inspector validates settings without connecting.
invoke inspect_database with a Channel<InspectionEvent>. The first event is Started{jobId}; Cancel calls cancel_inspection(jobId).

The whole job races the cancel token in tokio::select! (biased), connecting included. It opens a pool of up to 4 sessions and reads the server information. Then the access probe (stage CheckingAccess) and 7 set-based sys.* queries run together with tokio::try_join!, progress is reported, and assemble_snapshot builds the SchemaSnapshot with its access profile, NotVisible texts and keys to invisible tables. The pool is dropped.
syncRememberedPassword applies the 'Remember password' box: remember_password when it is ticked and a password was typed, forget_password when it was cleared for a stored one.
A snapshot whose access level is nothingVisible is not loaded: no project and no history entry. The dialog stays open with the blocking notice (blockedInspection) until the draft changes.
loadFromInspection: ensurePlaced, path null, liveSettings in memory, history cleared, loadToken + 1. A partial capture shows the access chip in the status bar and the access bar above the entities.
rememberConnection runs after the project exists and is not awaited; remember_connection writes preferences.json. A failure is only logged.
layoutFreshProject runs ELK in a worker and applies it with {undoable:false, dirty:false}, then fits the view.

flows.name: Start from the welcome screen or a recent item
flows.summary: Reopen a recent project in one click, or fill the connection form from the history.

steps.detail: On mount, preferencesStore.load() calls read_preferences and mirrors recentConnections and recentProjects.
While no project is open it renders the emptyState AppShell passes it, WelcomeOverlay: Connect, Open and up to 10 recent projects, each with projectDisplayName and projectDirectory.
projectStore.openProject(path) runs the unsaved-changes guard, then read_project as in the reopen flow. On project/notFound, forget_project removes the item.
The connection dialog lists recentConnections (never passwords). applyRecentConnection fills the draft with savedConnectionToDraft and clears the last test.
markStoredPassword calls has_stored_password and sets passwordIsStored and rememberPassword. With a stored password the field can stay empty and the form sends {source:'stored'}.
The connect and inspect flow continues from the test step.

flows.name: Trust an untrusted server certificate
flows.summary: The worked example of ADR-012: Rust classifies the failure, the UI offers the remedy.

steps.detail: Encryption is mandatory by default and the certificate is validated (trustServerCertificate false).
errors.rs turns the driver's TLS error into InspectorError::UntrustedCertificate. The host sends CommandError {kind: {type:'inspector', value:'untrustedCertificate'}, message}.
toOperationError normalises the rejection. failure.retry is 'test' or 'inspect', the step that failed.
describeOperationError returns the error.untrustedCertificate title and hint with offersCertificateTrust true, so the alert shows 'Trust the certificate and retry' instead of 'Retry'.
trustCertificateAndRetry sets trustServerCertificate = true in the draft and runs testConnection. If the inspection had failed and the test now passes, it runs inspect again.
The flag stays in the 'schemacraft.connection' draft and, after a successful inspection, in the history; the .scraft file keeps it once saved. Later sessions trust that server without asking.

flows.name: Save and reopen a project
flows.summary: Only the path crosses IPC; Rust writes and reads the file.

steps.detail: With no path yet, saveProjectAs opens the native save dialog with a .scraft filter.
invoke write_project {path, content}; phase 'saving'.

Project::from_content sets formatVersion 2, minReaderVersion 2, savedAt (now) and savedWith, drops header keys found in the content and normalises the canvas (nodes sorted by name); unknown keys are written back. write_json_atomically writes <file name>.tmp, e.g. northwind.scraft.tmp, then renames it.
isDirty false, savedAt set; remember_project adds the path.

steps.action: Reopens with Ctrl+O or a recent entry
steps.detail: The unsaved-changes guard runs first; then invoke read_project {path}.

Parses the JSON once and reads formatVersion and minReaderVersion first: a minReaderVersion above 2 is refused, a newer formatVersion opens read-only, format 1 is upgraded by migrations.rs; then the typed parse, which keeps unknown keys. A newer file that does not parse is UnsupportedFormatVersion. Errors: NotFound, Read, NotAProject, UnsupportedFormatVersion. Returns OpenedProject.

ensurePlaced, isReadOnly and savedWith from OpenedProject, liveSettings null, history cleared, loadToken + 1, saved viewport restored. No database contact. A read-only project shows the Read-only chip; Save, Save as and Refresh are unavailable and edits never mark it unsaved. On notFound the path leaves the recents; every failure shows in ProjectNotice.

flows.name: Close the window with unsaved changes
flows.summary: The title shows a dirty marker, and closing asks before work is lost.

steps.detail: On every change of path or isDirty it calls setWindowTitle: '• name – SchemaCraft' with unsaved changes, 'name – SchemaCraft' without, 'SchemaCraft' with no project. A project never saved uses the project.untitled text.
Title bar button, Alt+F4 or the taskbar. Tauri raises onCloseRequested in the webview.
Without unsaved changes the close goes ahead. With them, the handler given to watchWindowClose returns true and the close is cancelled (event.preventDefault()).
guardUnsavedChanges(proceed) stores proceed in pendingDiscard, and UnsavedChangesDialog opens.
Keep editing calls cancelDiscard and nothing closes. Discard changes calls confirmDiscard, which runs proceed.
closeWindow() calls window.destroy(), which closes the window without raising onCloseRequested again. This is why core:window:allow-destroy and allow-set-title are granted.

flows.name: Refresh with a reviewed diff
flows.summary: Re-read the database, review the changes, then apply them keeping positions.

steps.detail: connectionStore.refresh opens the dialog in mode 'refresh'. A read-only project is never refreshed.
Uses liveSettings if the session has them, so the typed password crosses IPC again; otherwise prefills from the saved connection and calls has_stored_password, or asks for the password.
inspect_database as in the connect flow returns a fresh snapshot.
compute_schema_diff -> SchemaDiff::between, which compares against the fresh snapshot merged with what it could not check (with_unchecked_facts_from); phase 'reviewing'.

Added, removed and changed tables, views, relations and keys to invisible tables; facts not checked, with the date they were read; facts now available; a change in what the login sees. A review with none of these offers only Close and says the project is up to date, or, under a partial capture, 'No changes in what this login can read'. Otherwise Apply is offered, worded 'Update project' when no object changed. Discard changes nothing.

refresh_project_content -> with_refreshed_snapshot applies the same merge, so the project keeps every fact the review listed as not checked (in snapshot.carriedOver), then keeps canvas state of surviving entities.
placeRefreshedEntities puts them next to related ones and highlights them, then ensurePlaced; isDirty true, history cleared, loadToken + 1. The file changes only when the user saves.

flows.name: Export a diagram
flows.summary: TypeScript draws the document; Rust renders and writes it.

steps.detail: exportStore.open preselects detail level and theme and measures the diagram.
Native save dialog with the format filter; ExportSpecificationBuilder.from(choices).to(destination).build().

Waits until document.fonts has the four static faces, so text is measured with them. renderDiagramSvg for SVG, PNG and PDF, with the VIEW label translated in the interface language (entity.view.label); for HTML, buildStandalonePage with the visibleProjection allowlist, the palette as --sc-* custom properties (viewerPaletteStyles) and virtual:schemacraft-viewer. A partial capture adds its one-line note. With embedFonts (SVG and HTML) the WOFF2 faces are inlined as base64.
export_diagram with a Channel<ExportEvent>; Started{jobId 'export-N'}; work runs on run_blocking.
Rendering (verbatim, resvg PNG or svg2pdf PDF, both with the bundled TTFs and the system fonts), one cancellation check, then Writing with write_bytes_atomically. Returns ExportOutcome.
revealItemInDir opens Explorer.

flows.name: Cut a release
flows.summary: Tag-driven, built without caches, published by hand after a checklist.

steps.detail: package.json and Cargo.toml workspace version, a dated CHANGELOG.md entry with its link, merged through a PR; CI fails a version without its entry.
git tag vX.Y.Z on main and push the tag.

The tag must be on main and equal 'v' + the package.json and Cargo.toml versions, and CHANGELOG.md must have its entry; all gates, npm run docs:check included; contracts check; npm run tauri build; WebView2 installed if missing; smoke test.

Renames assets to schemacraft-<tag>-windows-x64.exe and -setup.exe, writes SHA256SUMS.txt, creates a draft release whose notes are what SchemaCraft is, the assets and the code signing policy, then the CHANGELOG entry, followed by the generated list of pull requests.

Follows docs/release-checklist.md (checksums, clean machine, real database round trip, HTML in a browser, install and uninstall), then publishes. Builds are unsigned until SignPath approves (ADR-029).

flows.name: Inspect an entity
flows.summary: From a double-click, Enter or Ctrl+I to the selected table's details, with focus where it belongs.

steps.detail: Double-click on a card or on a row of the entities panel, Enter on a focused card, Ctrl+I (view.toggleInspector) or 'Show details' in the context menu. A double-click leaves focus where it was; Ctrl+I, the top-bar button, the palette, Enter on a focused card and 'Show details' (with the mouse too, because the closing menu leaves focus nowhere) ask for focus on the panel's heading (inspectorFocusRequest), and so does following a relation link. 'Show details' selects the entity without panning (focusEntity with center false); a hidden entity cannot be inspected, because it has no card to select.

openInspector sets isInspectorOpen and, when asked, bumps inspectorFocusRequest. The aside in AppShell leaves inert and widens to the remembered width (settingsStore.inspectorWidth), or to what fitSidePanels leaves it in a narrow window; nothing is saved.

inspectedKey(selectedKeys): one key shows the details; none or several show an empty state whose focus target is the permanent header. inspectorScope builds the DetailsScope from projectStore: the hidden nodes, the coverage from accessSummary, the carried facts and the schema filter.

describeObjectDetails reads the snapshot: columns, primary key, indexes, CHECKs, references and referenced by, each text as a FactText (readable, notAvailable, notRecorded, notChecked with its date, which a text inside an object kept whole takes from the object unless it was kept on its own) and each list with its ListCompleteness. presentObjectDetails translates it with useI18n's translator into a DetailsView; the same two calls serve the viewer over the embedded data.

One component per section kind, in the fixed order; 'None' only for a complete list; a relation target with a key is a link that runs focusEntity and openInspector({focus: true}), so the panel follows the new selection; a value the capture could not vouch for carries an icon and its hint; a not-available value, a not-visible target and a not-visible empty line add a 'Why?' link that opens the Access report (view.accessReport).

Escape anywhere in the panel, its resize handle included, returns focus to the inspected card (focusEntityNode) and leaves the panel open; the close button or Ctrl+I closes it, and returnFocusFromInspector hands focus back to the card or the canvas before the aside turns inert.

flows.name: Read a rule in words
flows.summary: From a CHECK or a foreign key to its sentences, with its columns highlighted on the canvas and its SQL one click away.

steps.detail: While building the details, describeObjectDetails reads each CHECK with readCheckConstraint (tokenizeCheck, parseCheck, then the closed set of forms, all or nothing, under 'When … has a value:' for nullable columns and 'When enabled:' for a disabled constraint) and explains each key with foreignKeyExplanation (whether it is required, how many rows can point to one row, ON DELETE and ON UPDATE, cached per snapshot). presentObjectDetails words both with formatRuleText into a RuleView per item and adds the section notes.

The sentences with column, table and code chips and their group headings, or the line that says the rule cannot be put into words, with its stored SQL open; Show SQL reveals the SQL, its note and Copy SQL.
Hovers the item, or reaches one of its controls with Tab (the SQL toggle, Copy SQL, the target link): the highlight adds no tab stop.

setRuleHighlight({owner, columns, edgeId}) replaces any earlier one; clearRuleHighlight(owner) clears it only for the item that set it, once neither the pointer nor the focus is inside; closeInspector and a real change of selection clear it as well.

Each card reads only its own entry: an accent outline 3 px off the card, and the rule's shown rows tinted with an accent bar; a key's line is emphasised without opening its label. The Inspector's columns table tints the same rows.

steps.action: Does the same in the file
steps.detail: rules.ts draws the same RuleView with a <details> for the SQL; pointing at a rule paints the sc-rule-* outline, tint and classes, found through data-column and data-relation, and render() repaints them after a change of theme or detail level.
