patterns.name: Framework-free core
patterns.why: Logic is testable without Tauri or a UI (ADR-001).

patterns.name: Thin adapter commands
patterns.why: Commands resolve inputs, call the core and map errors; no domain logic in the host.

patterns.name: Strategy: DatabaseInspector
patterns.why: Engines plug in behind one trait and the create_inspector factory (PRD 4.3).

patterns.name: Strategy: CredentialStore
patterns.why: System store in the app, in-memory store in tests (ADR-019).

patterns.name: Strategy: layouts
patterns.why: runLayout switches on a tagged LayoutRequest; lint enforces exhaustiveness; ELK runs in a worker (ADR-022).

patterns.name: Builder
patterns.why: ExportSpecificationBuilder validates and normalises export choices in one place.

patterns.name: Memento
patterns.why: CanvasState is an immutable value; projectStore keeps up to 100 for undo and redo (ADR-021).

patterns.name: Backend resolver
patterns.why: Picks Tauri, DEV preview or unavailable per window, so the UI runs in a plain browser too (ADR-014, ADR-018).

patterns.name: Generated contracts
patterns.why: Rust types generate the TypeScript; CI blocks drift (ADR-003).

patterns.name: One renderer, two outputs
patterns.why: The same SVG renderer and canvas geometry serve every export and the HTML viewer (ADR-023, ADR-025).

patterns.name: TS draws, Rust writes
patterns.why: Only a document string crosses IPC; Rust rasterises and writes (ADR-024).

patterns.name: Action registry (Command)
patterns.why: Toolbar, shortcuts and palette share one list of operations (ADR-008).

patterns.name: Typed errors with kinds
patterns.why: Rust classifies; the UI owns the localised remedy, such as 'Trust the certificate and retry' (ADR-012).

patterns.name: Allowlist of typed log events
patterns.why: The log file takes only events whose parameters cannot carry a name, a path or code, through a formatter that writes no span, so it can be shared without reading it twice (ADR-041).

patterns.name: Long-running job
patterns.why: Jobs registry, Channel with Started{jobId} first, cancel_* command. Async jobs race the token, connecting included; blocking jobs check it between steps (ADR-013).

patterns.name: Atomic write
patterns.why: Temp file, sync_all, then rename, so a crash or a power cut never leaves a half-written file (ADR-015).

patterns.name: Rust owns state, frontend mirrors
patterns.why: One source of truth for history (ADR-017).

patterns.name: Per-operation pool
patterns.why: No idle sessions on production servers (ADR-009).

patterns.name: Pure functional core
patterns.why: Deterministic, sorted output that is unit tested without a database or a DOM.

patterns.name: Store per stateful feature
patterns.why: State and async actions live together; components use narrow selectors. schema has no store, and canvas edits go through projectStore.updateCanvas.

patterns.name: Guarded close
patterns.why: The window never closes over unsaved changes without asking; the title shows '•' while they exist.

patterns.name: WebView2 preflight
patterns.why: A missing runtime gets a native bilingual message and the download page instead of a blank window (ADR-010).

patterns.name: Tag-driven release
patterns.why: A v* tag builds, smoke-tests and drafts the release; a person publishes it after the checklist (ADR-027). Signing waits for SignPath (ADR-029).

patterns.name: Same fonts everywhere
patterns.why: The canvas, the measured SVG, the embedded fonts and the PNG and PDF renderer use the same four faces, so exports match the screen (ADR-024).

patterns.name: Checked architecture model
patterns.why: The page is data plus a renderer; CI compares its manifest with the code (ADR-030).

patterns.name: Lint-enforced layers
patterns.why: no-restricted-imports per folder keeps app -> features -> shared and the Tauri API inside shared/ipc (ADR-031).

patterns.name: Blocking work off the main thread
patterns.why: run_blocking moves file, keyring and heavy work to the blocking pool, so no command freezes the window (ADR-032).

patterns.name: Graded disclosure
patterns.why: Full access adds nothing; partial access gets a chip, a dismissible bar and 'not available' where the user looks, and nothing is called absent unless coverage is complete (ADR-034).

patterns.name: Carry-over on refresh
patterns.why: A login that sees less removes nothing: unchecked facts are kept and listed as not checked, the same in the review and in the project (ADR-016, ADR-034).

patterns.name: Forward-compatible reader
patterns.why: formatVersion and minReaderVersion decide between upgrade, read-only and refusal, and unknown keys survive a save (ADR-035).

patterns.name: Shared view-model, two renderers
patterns.why: The Inspector and the viewer's detail panel draw one DetailsView, so the application and the exported file say the same about an object and 'None' is printed only for a complete list (ADR-038).

patterns.name: Interpreter over a closed grammar with conservative fallback
patterns.why: A CHECK is put into words only when every part of it is a known form; anything else shows the stored SQL, so a reading can say too little but never something false (ADR-039).

patterns.name: Sentences as data
patterns.why: The readers return message keys with typed arguments, never text, so both languages and both renderers word one reading and a column becomes a chip without concatenation (ADR-007, ADR-039).

patterns.name: Golden table checked against the engine
patterns.why: One file of written, stored and expected forms drives the Rust test against SQL Server and the reader's tests, so a normal form that changes fails CI before a sentence goes wrong (ADR-039).

featureTypes.example: A panel beside the canvas, built like features/inspector (ADR-038), or a dialog, built like features/about.

steps.step: If it adds scope, update the PRD in both copies with a dated line in section 6, commit as docs(prd), and get approval.
files: master copy of the PRD outside the repository

steps.step: Create src/features/<feature>/ with a component, its CSS Module, a <feature>Store.ts if it holds state, and pure logic modules. No new barrel index.ts (src/shared/contracts/index.ts and canvas/layouts/index.ts are the existing exceptions).

Use narrow selectors on projectStore and canvasUiStore. Reuse entityKey, EntityKind, listEntities and groupEntities (features/schema/entities.ts, the one home of entity identity), describeEntities and formatDataType, and describeObjectDetails with presentObjectDetails for an entity's details, so a panel says what the viewer says. Call other stores with getState().
Build from shared/ui and lucide icons; style with tokens only: a new colour is a token in tokens.css first, and tokens.test.ts fails on a raw colour in a CSS Module.

Mount once in AppShell: a side panel in its own aside landmark, inert while closed, with a PanelResizer from shared/ui and its width in settingsStore, as the Inspector; something over the canvas in features/canvas/DiagramCanvas.tsx (as ProjectNotice does; the welcome screen arrives through the emptyState prop). A non-modal panel must not use role="dialog", because open dialogs block shortcuts, and must hand focus back to the canvas when it closes while holding it (returnFocusFromInspector shows how).
Open or toggle it through an AppAction (see the action recipe).
Only if it changes the diagram: a pure with*() in canvasState.ts and a command in canvasActions.ts through updateCanvas.
Add keys to en.ts and es.ts, expose the store in developmentHooks.ts, and test pure modules with vitest.
Key flow in ux-principles.md, README 'Features', architecture.md layout, this page's model (npm run docs:check), CHANGELOG.

featureTypes.example: Column and table descriptions from MS_Description, shown on cards, in the review and in the HTML viewer.

steps.step: Add the data to PRD 3.2 in both copies and get approval.

Add the field as Option or Vec with #[serde(default)] so old .scraft files still open. If a login may lack the right to read it, keep 'not visible' apart from 'none' (a Definition, or an Option documented as such) and decide how AccessCounts and the coverage count it. Derive serde camelCase and TS, add /// docs, update sample_snapshot and reader_snapshot.
Add a named CatalogQuery (fixed, set-based SELECT over sys.*), a row struct, a mapper, a CatalogRows field and one more fetch_stage in try_join!.
Group by object_id in a BTreeMap, honour the filter, sort, attach to the model. Unit test with hand-built rows.

Decide if a change shows in the review: a ColumnProperty, a new list on TableChange::Changed, or a ForeignKeyProperty. Compare texts only when both are readable (differs_from), and decide what with_unchecked_facts_from keeps when the fresh capture cannot see the data.

A new per-entity fact raises FORMAT_VERSION, with a step in migrations.rs and a fixture file of the previous format; a new value of a closed enum also raises MIN_READER_VERSION (ADR-035). Test that the older file upgrades and saves, and update sample_project_content.
npm run contracts and commit the generated files.
No change while the data travels inside SchemaSnapshot.
Add the data to previewSnapshot, sampleProject and fabricatedChanges, and to every test literal of Table or Column.

Show it in EntityNode.tsx and ReviewChangesPanel.tsx, draw it in renderDiagram.ts and the viewer, with 'not available' when the capture could not read it. visibleProjection is an allowlist: the data reaches HTML only if it is added there on purpose.

Start a local server with scripts/dev-sqlserver.ps1 start and load its env, then the same with -Version 2019, since CI reads both versions. Seed fixture.sql and changes.sql and assert in sqlserver_integration.rs, and add the data to permissions.sql with an assertion per affected login in sqlserver_permissions.rs. Keep the 200-table test (stress_200_tables.sql) under 5 s.
Update ADR-009 (query count), ADR-034 if visibility rules change, ADR-016 or ADR-035 if their rules change, README, ux-principles.md, CHANGELOG and this page's model.

featureTypes.example: A Mermaid or DBML text export (TS builds, Rust writes verbatim) or a JPEG raster (Rust renders from SVG).

steps.step: Add the format to PRD 3.7 in both copies.

Add an ExportFormat variant. Verbatim formats join the Svg | Html arm; rendered ones get a function in render.rs that validates before allocating and uses font_database() from fonts.rs. Keep write_bytes_atomically.
New crates go in [workspace.dependencies], AGPL-compatible (ADR-028); respect the resvg/usvg 0.45 pin.
npm run contracts.

EXPORT_FORMATS and FILE_EXTENSIONS, the build() normalisation (embedFonts applies only to SVG and HTML), buildDocument, estimateFileBytes, FORMAT_ICONS and the per-format branches in ExportDialog.tsx; i18n keys export.format.<f>, export.format.<f>.hint and export.file.<f> (the save-dialog file type); the preview export backend.
ADR-023/024 or a new ADR, the 'Exporting' key flow, README, CHANGELOG, this page.

featureTypes.kind: New user action with a shortcut

steps.step: A pure transform in canvasState.ts (return the same object on a no-op) and a command in canvasActions.ts through updateCanvas.
Add the id to ActionId and the entry in useAppActions (labelKey, icon, shortcut {mod, shift, alt, key}, isAvailable, skipWhenEditing, run). Add new selectors to the useMemo deps.

Avoid taken keys and reserved browser keys (shortcut.ts). The first match wins; useAppActions.test.ts builds the registry and fails on a duplicate shortcut or on a browser key that is not on its claimed list, so a deliberately reused key is added there. A gesture on one entity, or Enter on a card, is not a registry shortcut (ADR-008).
Add action.<name> in both catalogues; place an ActionIconButton if needed. The palette lists it automatically.
'Working on the canvas' key flow, ADR-026 if a browser key is claimed, CHANGELOG.

featureTypes.example: A colour or note per table that survives save, undo and refresh.

steps.step: Add the field to NodeState or CanvasState with #[serde(default)]; check normalized() and retaining_entities_of; test defaults and a round trip that is byte-stable apart from savedAt. Older versions keep it as an unknown key; raise FORMAT_VERSION only if it depends on content they could change (ADR-035).
npm run contracts.

A pure with<Thing>() and a command through updateCanvas. Update the NodeState literals in canvasState.ts (ensurePlaced) and refreshPlacement.ts, and defaultCanvasState in projectStore.ts. Show it on the canvas, in renderDiagram.ts (a token in tokens.css plus its palette.ts entry, which tokens.test.ts checks) and in the viewer.
ADR-015 and ADR-021, key flows, CHANGELOG.

featureTypes.example: Any new operation the UI asks Rust to do.

steps.step: A core function with a thiserror enum and a TS-exported *ErrorKind.

A #[tauri::command] in a commands module, registered in generate_handler!. Keep it synchronous only if it just reads memory; otherwise make it async and run file, credential-store or heavy work through run_blocking (ADR-032). A new error type gets a CommandErrorKind variant and From impl. A long job uses Jobs, a Channel and a cancel_* command.
A capability entry only if a plugin or window API is used, naming the exact permission rather than a :default set.
npm run contracts; a backend interface with Tauri, preview and unavailable implementations via createBackendResolver, calling commands through invokeCommand; error keys error.<name>.title and .hint.
An ADR, and this page's command list and manifest.commands (npm run docs:check fails until both are updated).
A new module under inspectors/ implementing DatabaseInspector, and a ConnectionSettings variant (inspectors/settings.rs) matched in create_inspector (inspectors/mod.rs).
A SavedConnection variant and a CredentialKey constructor. Today project/connection.rs imports SQL Server types; the inspectors doc lists every such part.
Draft, form and conversions that hard-code provider 'sqlServer', plus i18n keys.

crossCutting.touches: en.ts is the reference, es.ts typed as MessageCatalog, catalogs.test.ts. The viewer says the subset an export embeds (viewerMessages, by key prefix; viewerMessages.test.ts checks it) through the same createCatalogTranslator and has no catalogue of its own (ADR-007); the WebView2 dialog text is in src-tauri/src/main.rs. The words of the readable rules are a sub-catalogue, messages/rules/en.ts and es.ts, spread into both and embedded by the rule. prefix; sentences are built from templates with formatMessageParts and Intl.ListFormat, never concatenated, and name tables as tables, never as nouns guessed from their names (ADR-039).

tokens.css with light-dark() is the only source of colour. src/features/export/svg/palette.ts is its sRGB derivation, checked by src/app/styles/tokens.test.ts, which also refuses a raw hex or oklch() colour in any CSS Module or in viewer.css (the viewer keeps only its two translucent shadows); buildStandalonePage writes the palette into the HTML as --sc-* properties (ADR-037).

src/app/actions; dialogs block shortcuts, a non-modal panel such as the Inspector does not; plain keys never fire in text fields; Enter on a card is handled by the canvas and per-entity gestures call feature functions, not actions, and the controls of a rule are local to its item, whose highlight follows the focus without an extra tab stop (ADR-008, ADR-039).

Only CanvasState is undoable, through projectStore.updateCanvas; transient state (the selection, the Inspector's open state, the rule it highlights) goes in canvasUiStore. The window title shows '•' and closing asks first (useProjectWindow).

FORMAT_VERSION 2 and MIN_READER_VERSION 2; upgrades on the raw JSON in migrations.rs; newer files open read-only; unknown keys kept at the root, the snapshot, the canvas and each node. When to raise each number is in ADR-035.

crates/schemacraft-core/src/diff and model/carry_over.rs (not checked, now available, access changed), ReviewChangesPanel.tsx with isUpToDate, refreshPlacement.ts, withUncheckedFacts and fabricatedChanges in the preview backends.

Shared geometry, one marker and routing table (canvas/edgeGeometry.ts) whose ends relationEnds picks for every surface, and one palette; the renderer takes its labels from the caller, so a view reads VIEW or VISTA in the export's language; visibleProjection is an allowlist that decides what reaches HTML (never the probe, the database user, a hidden table's facts or unknown keys; the verdicts, the read dates of the kept facts of the objects on the diagram and the viewer's message subset travel apart from the snapshot); the viewer's detail panel is the Inspector's view-model, so both use the same words and states, the file only for what is on the diagram (ADR-038); a partial capture carries one note line; the viewer reads the rules with the same readers and finds their columns through data-column (ADR-039).
Keep previewSnapshot, the access scenarios (server names with partial, nothing or empty), the sample projects, previewAccess.ts and fabricatedChanges current in src/shared/ipc.

Core *ErrorKind -> CommandErrorKind -> toOperationError -> error.<name>.title/hint. For the diagnostic log, log_summary() -> CommandError (error number and query, never serialised) -> CommandError::log, through commands::logged.
Jobs, Channel, Started{jobId} first, cancel_* returning UnknownJob; async jobs race the token, connecting included (ADR-013).

A new event is a function in crates/schemacraft-core/src/diagnostics.rs whose parameters are numbers, booleans, durations, &'static str or ClosedKind values; no other file emits on its target (source scan test). A new error enum gets log_summary() and a ClosedKind kind; a new command wraps its body in commands::logged. Extend tests/diagnostics_privacy.rs when a new path reads the server (ADR-041).

No app database; four persistence places, plus the local diagnostic log of typed events (ADR-041); passwords as SecretString and never in files, but a typed one crosses IPC on every connection call; the connection draft keeps trustServerCertificate; .scraft stores the database user name, which exports never embed; strict CSP (devCsp only for tauri dev) and capabilities.

app -> features -> shared and the Tauri API only in shared/ipc, enforced by ESLint no-restricted-imports (ADR-031); features/schema imports only shared/ and itself, so the viewer can take it (ADR-037); core never depends on Tauri.
150 tables in under 3 s (PRD 4.1), 200-table test in 5 s, 60 fps canvas, ELK in a worker.
Commands that only read memory stay synchronous; every other command is async and runs file, credential-store and heavy work through run_blocking in src-tauri/src/commands/mod.rs (ADR-032).

main.tsx loads the static @fontsource faces that the exporter measures; fontFaces.ts embeds them in SVG and HTML; scripts/prepare-fonts.mjs turns the same faces into the TTFs in crates/schemacraft-core/assets/fonts for PNG and PDF. Bump the packages, run the script and commit the TTFs together.

A login may see part of a database (ADR-034). Whatever lists or counts schema facts asks src/features/schema/coverage.ts before it says 'none', and an unreadable text reads 'not available'; the Inspector and the viewer's detail panel print 'None' only for a complete list and mark every fact the capture could not vouch for (ADR-038); a key to a table the login cannot see is worded against 'the referenced table', with no SQL (ADR-039). The server side is covered by the logins in sqlserver_permissions.rs; the browser preview reproduces it with a server name that contains partial.

crossCutting.concern: Teach the rule reader a CHECK form
crossCutting.touches: Add a case to crates/schemacraft-core/tests/fixtures/sqlserver/check_forms.json: as written, as stored, the columns it reads in order and the expected reading, or 'unread' with why. Run the SQL Server integration test against the local container (dev-sqlserver.ps1), which pins the stored form; add the rule.check.* keys to src/shared/i18n/messages/rules/en.ts and es.ts; teach checkReader.ts the form, leaving it unread wherever NULL, the collation, the session or a conversion could make the sentence false; run checkReader.test.ts, which reads every golden case (ADR-039).

definitionOfDone: Plan approved by the user before code; PRD updated in both copies if scope changes.
npm run format:check, lint, typecheck, test and docs:check pass.
cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings and cargo test --workspace pass; no unwrap, expect or panic in production code.
Contracts regenerated and committed.
Unit tests beside new pure modules; catalog or diff changes have SQL Server integration tests.
Older .scraft files still open, and newer ones open read-only (ADR-035).
Data features checked with a login that sees part of the schema: 'not available' instead of empty, nothing called absent.
en.ts and es.ts complete.
UX definition of done: action with tooltip and shortcut, loading/empty/error states, both themes, both languages, keyboard only, WCAG AA.
Export parity checked and no private data leaks into HTML.
Verified in the browser preview and in the desktop app; data features against a real SQL Server.
CI green on the PR: Windows job and Linux integration job.
Docs updated in the same PR: ADRs, architecture.md layout, ux-principles.md, README, CHANGELOG, this page's model.
Branch from main, Conventional Commits, merge commit through a PR, never auto-merge.

conventions.rule: Rust: full English words, verb-first functions, intent-named constructors. TS: PascalCase.tsx components with a PascalCase.module.css, camelCase.ts logic, <feature>Store.ts, use<Thing>.ts hooks.

src/app composes src/features, and both use src/shared; shared never imports app or features, and ESLint enforces it (ADR-031). One folder per capability: code several features need moves down into shared, code that composes the application moves up into app.

One thiserror enum per core domain with kind() returning a TS-exported *ErrorKind. Each also has log_summary() for the diagnostic log: kind, SQL Server error number and query name, never the message. The host wraps it in CommandError. The UI writes the user text.
clippy denies unwrap, expect, panic, todo, unimplemented and dbg_macro; unsafe is forbidden; CI uses -D warnings. Only test modules opt out.
Every public Rust item has a /// doc, enforced by missing_docs with clippy -D warnings. Crate roots and mod.rs files carry a //! header.
Edit the Rust type, run npm run contracts, commit. Never edit generated files.
Features call getXBackend() and the wrappers in src/shared/ipc, never invoke or @tauri-apps/* directly; ESLint enforces it.
Synchronous only when a command just reads memory; otherwise async, with blocking work in run_blocking (ADR-032).
Stateful features own one zustand store; schema is a pure helper module; async state is a phase plus a failure; canvas edits go only through projectStore.updateCanvas.

A fact the login could not read is recorded as such (Definition notVisible, foreignKeysToInvisibleTables, partial coverage) and shown as 'not available'; a list says 'none' only under complete coverage. Wording: 'not visible to this login', never 'hidden', which means hidden on the canvas (ADR-034). A rule SchemaCraft cannot read in full shows its SQL, never a partial sentence (ADR-039).

All user text in en.ts and es.ts (the rule words in the messages/rules sub-catalogue they spread in); plurals with .one/.other and tCount; no string concatenation: a sentence with chips is built with formatMessageParts.
Tokens from tokens.css through CSS Modules; no raw colours.

Rust tests in #[cfg(test)] mod tests beside the code; vitest *.test.ts beside pure modules; SQL Server tests gated by SCHEMACRAFT_TEST_MSSQL_*, which fail instead of skipping under SCHEMACRAFT_TEST_REQUIRE_SERVER.
Conventional Commits, e.g. feat(core), feat(app), feat(ui), docs, test(core); the body names the ADRs.
Branch from main. main accepts only merge commits through PRs with both CI checks green and up to date (ruleset 'Protect main').
One pull request per coherent block of work, with one commit per logical part; a separate small one only for an urgent fix to something released. CI runs what the change needs (ADR-033).

conformance.verdict: The architecture holds. The core has no Tauri dependency, commands are thin and keep blocking work off the main thread, errors are typed end to end, contracts are generated and checked, ESLint enforces the frontend layers and keeps features/schema a leaf, only src/shared/ipc talks to Tauri, and the viewer pulls in no React or stores. Builder and Memento are implemented as the ADRs say, and each drawing rule has one home guarded by a test. Every deviation is fixed, the three major ones included, the last being the log file for bug reports (ADR-041). Fixed entries stay below, marked fixed.

deviations.fix: Fixed: AppAction has unavailableReason, useAppActions fills it (no project, layout running, nothing hidden, nothing to undo or redo) and common.comingSoon is gone.

deviations.fix: Fixed: src/shared/ipc/invokeCommand.ts is the one copy; every backend and appInfo.ts use it.

deviations.fix: Fixed: src/shared/ipc/nativeWindow.ts wraps the title, the close guard and destroy; useProjectWindow no longer imports Tauri.
